name: Prometheus
tagline: Pulls metrics on an interval, stores them, answers PromQL, fires alerts.

howItWorks.title: Pull scraping
howItWorks.body:
Every scrape_interval, an HTTP GET fetches /metrics from each target.
Targets come from static lists, DNS, file or Kubernetes service discovery.
A failed scrape sets up to 0: free health checking.
relabel_configs picks targets; metric_relabel_configs drops series.

howItWorks.title: node_exporter and Actuator
howItWorks.body:
node_exporter reads /proc and /sys: CPU, memory, disk, network per host.
Spring Boot Actuator serves JVM and HTTP metrics at /actuator/prometheus.
Micrometer publishes http_server_requests_seconds histograms per URI and status.
Saturation comes from nodes; latency and errors come from the app.

howItWorks.title: ServiceMonitor and OTel push
howItWorks.body:
A ServiceMonitor selects Services by label and sets port, path, interval.
The Operator turns it into scrape config; teams ship it with their app.
Where pull is impossible, the OTel Collector pushes via remote_write.
The receiver needs --web.enable-remote-write-receiver.

howItWorks.title: Histograms and p95
howItWorks.body:
Histograms expose cumulative _bucket{le} counters plus _sum and _count.
p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(x_bucket[5m]))).
Aggregate buckets with sum by (le) first, then take the quantile.
Summaries cannot be aggregated across pods; prefer histograms.
Bucket edges must bracket the SLO threshold, or p95 is guesswork.

howItWorks.title: Alerts and long-term storage
howItWorks.body:
Alert rules hold a PromQL condition for a duration, then fire.
Alertmanager groups, deduplicates, silences, inhibits and routes by label.
Recording rules precompute expensive queries for fast dashboards.
Thanos sidecar uploads sealed 2h blocks to object storage.
Thanos Query merges live and stored data; local retention stays short.

howItWorks.title: What sits in front
howItWorks.body:
Targets sit in front: node_exporter, application endpoints at /metrics and other exporters.
Service discovery lists targets: static files, DNS, Consul or the Kubernetes API.
Short-lived jobs push to a Pushgateway, which Prometheus then scrapes.
Prometheus pulls over HTTP; Users and the Edge never see these ports.

howItWorks.title: What sits behind
howItWorks.body:
Grafana adds Prometheus as a datasource on port 9090 and runs PromQL against it.
Alertmanager on port 9093 receives alerts and routes them to Slack, email or paging tools.
Remote write ships samples to long-term storage such as Thanos or Mimir.
On Kubernetes, kube-prometheus-stack installs the Operator, Prometheus, Alertmanager and Grafana together.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
VictoriaMetrics: choose it for lower memory use and simpler long-term storage.
Datadog or other SaaS: choose it when you want no servers to operate.
OpenTelemetry Collector: choose it to receive pushed metrics from many sources.
Thanos or Mimir: add them for global query and long retention, not as a replacement.

flow: node_exporter and Actuator expose /metrics over HTTP.
ServiceMonitor tells the Operator which Services to scrape.
Prometheus scrapes each target and appends samples to the WAL.
Two-hour blocks compact to disk; the Thanos sidecar uploads them.
Recording rules precompute; alert rules evaluate each interval.
Firing alerts go to Alertmanager, then Slack, email or pager.
Grafana runs PromQL; histogram_quantile returns p95.

deploy.summary: Prometheus, Alertmanager and node_exporter on a Linux host, pinned, with rules and a ServiceMonitor.
prerequisites: Linux host with Docker 24+ and Compose v2

steps.title: node_exporter under systemd
steps.code:
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/prometheus/node_exporter/releases/download/v1.8.1/node_exporter-1.8.1.linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar xzf node_exporter-1.8.1.linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 node_exporter-1.8.1.linux-amd64/node_exporter /usr/local/bin/
sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin node_exporter
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/node_exporter.service >/dev/null <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Prometheus node_exporter
After=network-online.target
[Service]
User=node_exporter
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node_exporter --web.listen-address=:9100
Restart=on-failure
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now node_exporter
steps.note: Runs unprivileged on every host. Use the arm64 tarball on ARM.

steps.title: Firewall: scrape from Prometheus only
steps.code:
# 10.0.0.5 = Prometheus host (placeholder)
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.5 to any port 9100 proto tcp
sudo ufw status numbered
steps.note: Replace 10.0.0.5 with your Prometheus address. On that host, allow 9090 and 9093 only from admin subnets.

steps.title: Compose: Prometheus and Alertmanager
steps.code:
services:
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.53.0
    command:
      - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=15d
      - --web.enable-lifecycle
      - --web.enable-remote-write-receiver
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./rules.yml:/etc/prometheus/rules.yml:ro
      - prom-data:/prometheus
    ports: ["9090:9090"]
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.27.0
    command: ["--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml"]
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
    ports: ["9093:9093"]
networks:
  default:
    name: monitoring
volumes:
  prom-data: {}
steps.note: Save as docker-compose.yml; drop the remote-write flag if nothing pushes. Grafana joins the same network.

steps.title: prometheus.yml
steps.code:
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s
  evaluation_interval: 15s
rule_files:
  - /etc/prometheus/rules.yml
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - static_configs:
        - targets: ["alertmanager:9093"]
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: prometheus
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["localhost:9090"]
  - job_name: node
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["<NODE_IP>:9100"]
  - job_name: spring-app
    metrics_path: /actuator/prometheus
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["<APP_IP>:8080"]
steps.note: Replace <NODE_IP> and <APP_IP>. Static targets here; use file or Kubernetes discovery at scale.

steps.title: Recording and alert rules
steps.code:
groups:
  - name: http
    rules:
      - record: job:http_requests:rate5m
        expr: sum by (job) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count[5m]))
      - record: job:http_request_duration_seconds:p95
        expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (job, le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket[5m])))
      - alert: HighP95Latency
        expr: job:http_request_duration_seconds:p95 > 0.5
        for: 10m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "p95 latency above 500ms for {{ $labels.job }}"
  - name: availability
    rules:
      - alert: TargetDown
        expr: up == 0
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "{{ $labels.job }}/{{ $labels.instance }} is down"
steps.note: p95 is precomputed per job. The 10 minute hold avoids flapping.

steps.title: Alertmanager routing
steps.code:
route:
  receiver: default
  group_by: [alertname, job]
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  routes:
    - matchers: [severity="critical"]
      receiver: oncall
receivers:
  - name: default
  - name: oncall
    webhook_configs:
      - url: http://host.docker.internal:5001/alerts
inhibit_rules:
  - source_matchers: [severity="critical"]
    target_matchers: [severity="warning"]
    equal: [job]
steps.note: Critical pages on-call and inhibits the matching warning. Webhook URL is a placeholder.

steps.title: Validate, start, reload
steps.code:
docker run --rm --entrypoint promtool -v "$PWD":/w prom/prometheus:v2.53.0 check config /w/prometheus.yml
docker run --rm --entrypoint promtool -v "$PWD":/w prom/prometheus:v2.53.0 check rules /w/rules.yml
docker compose up -d
curl -X POST http://localhost:9090/-/reload
steps.note: promtool fails the pipeline before a bad rule ships. Reload needs --web.enable-lifecycle.

steps.title: ServiceMonitor on Kubernetes
steps.code:
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: spring-app
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spring-app
  endpoints:
    - port: http
      path: /actuator/prometheus
      interval: 15s
steps.note: The release label must match the Operator's selector. Port names the Service port.

verify: Rules load: docker run --rm --entrypoint promtool -v "$PWD":/w prom/prometheus:v2.53.0 check rules /w/rules.yml
pitfalls: Averaging quantiles across pods is wrong; sum buckets by le first.
High-cardinality labels (user id, URL with IDs) explode memory.
rate() window under 4x the scrape interval returns gaps.
Pushgateway keeps stale series forever; delete them or avoid it.
No for: duration on alerts causes flapping pages.
ServiceMonitor ignored when its labels miss the Operator's selector.
Local TSDB is not durable storage: add Thanos or remote_write.
keyPoints: Pull model: scrape /metrics every interval; up==0 means dead.
Histograms plus histogram_quantile give p95 across all pods.
Cardinality, not sample rate, drives memory and cost.
Prometheus fires, Alertmanager groups, silences and routes.
osiNote: Scrapes over HTTP on TCP; reads kernel network counters.
production: Size memory by active series; cap with sample_limit.
Run HA pairs with identical config; Thanos sidecar uploads blocks.
Keep rules and config in Git; gate reloads on promtool checks.
Restrict /metrics by firewall or mTLS; never expose Prometheus publicly.
Alert on up==0, rule failures, scrape duration and WAL errors.
